text:
sara: FYI — BlueCove's renewal conversation moved up to next Tuesday. I need a concise cost + token econ snapshot and a spend forecast we can show the account team. Can folks run a quick preflight?

mike_cs: On it. Is there a preferred forecast window? 30/60/90 days? Also, any changes in their usage pattern we should account for?

sara: 60 days is ideal. They ramped an embeddings-heavy workflow last month (approx +35% tokens/day). Renewal ask is for predictable spend and a recommended guardrail.

raj: I can pull a baseline from billing for the last 45 days and run a simple burn projection. Need the current tokens-per-call and per-embedding unit assumptions.

lynne: @raj current config for BlueCove: text-gen model = rwd-medium-q4 (cost profile: 0.0006 $/1k tokens gen), embeddings = rwd-embed-v2 (0.0004 $/1k embed-units). Avg tokens per request ~120 for gen, ~1.2 embed-units per embedding call. Caching hasn't been enabled for their prefix routes.

mike_cs: Good call on caching. If we enable prefix KV caching on their search pipeline we can shave ~20-30% of gen tokens for repeated user prompts. That should help the forecast.

tom_oncall: Quick experiment suggestion: run cost sim with and without prefix cache + a 10% uplift scenario to simulate campaign spike. I'll kick off the sim if you drop the params.

sara: Params: account=BlueCove, window=60, baseline_tokens_per_day=1.2M, spike_multiplier=1.1, enable_cache=false then true. Can we get both CSVs by EOD?

raj: I'll export billing slice and run the sim. Using our internal sim script: 
```
./tools/cost_sim --account BlueCove --days 60 --tokens-per-day 1200000 --spike 1.1 --cache false --out bluecove_no_cache.csv
./tools/cost_sim --account BlueCove --days 60 --tokens-per-day 1200000 --spike 1.1 --cache true --out bluecove_cache.csv
```
I'll push results to the shared folder.

mike_cs: Also adding a simple token-econ slide: current monthly burn, projected 60-day spend, estimated savings with cache, and a recommended guardrail (alerts at +15% weekly burn).

sara: Perfect. Can someone validate model unit costs? We don't want surprise deltas because of a recent price change.

lynne: Confirmed: no rate card changes for their models in the last 90 days. The sim should use the following unit costs: gen=0.0006 $/1k, embed=0.0004 $/1k. I'll attach the small table to the deck.

cost-bot: [usage-alert] BlueCove: 24h token variance +42% vs rolling 7d average — origin: embeddings pipeline — triggered at 2026-03-16T18:12:03Z

mike_cs: Thanks @cost-bot — that's the ramp. Raj, factor that recent variance into a near-term spike scenario (we already included 1.1, maybe run 1.3 for sensitivity).

raj: Running 1.3 now as a second sensitivity. ETA ~40m.

tom_oncall: I'll prepare an enablement dry-run deck slide with talking points: what caused the spike, short-term mitigation (cache + rate limiter), mid-term recommendation (batching + reserved capacity), and ask (commit to a stabilized run-rate or consider Dedicated pool).

sara: Also capture renewal risk level: if predicted 60-day cost > +25% vs baseline we'll flag high risk and recommend a follow-up pricing conversation.

mike_cs: Agreed. I'll also prepare an action checklist for the customer call: 1) share incremental savings from cache, 2) propose 2-week trial of prefix caching, 3) propose alert thresholds and a runbook, 4) schedule technical deep-dive if they accept.

lynne: One more thing: let's include a short sample prompt set and the eval delta (quality vs quantized model) so they feel comfortable with a potential quantization recommendation. I'll run an eval on a 20-sample prompt set.

raj: Results uploaded: bluecove_no_cache.csv, bluecove_cache.csv, bluecove_sensitivity_1_3.csv (shared folder: /shared/customer/BlueCove/qbr/). Summary: cache scenario shows ~26% reduction in gen token volume over the 60-day projection for repeated flows; sensitivity 1.3 pushes 60-day spend to +28% vs baseline.

mike_cs: That's the trigger. With no cache and 1.3 spike we cross the +25% renewal-risk threshold. Good to have numbers.

sara: Can someone draft a 1-page summary for the account execs? Need: headline (risk=yes/no), numbers, recommended mitigation, next steps.

tom_oncall: I'll do the first draft and drop it in the folder. Expect it in ~1h.

mike_cs: I'll prep the slide with charts. LYNNE — once your eval is done, can you add a short note comparing gen quality with a 4-bit quantized variant? Execs will ask.

lynne: Will do. Early check: quantized q4 shows negligible quality regression on the 20-sample set, latency improves ~12%. I'll add concrete numbers.

sara: Amazing — thanks everyone. Final deliverables checklist: 1) EOD cost CSVs (raj) 2) sensitivity runs (raj) 3) 1-page summary (tom) 4) slide deck + charts (mike_cs) 5) eval note (lynne) 6) runbook/alert thresholds (mike_cs). If we hit all of that we can run the enablement dry-run tomorrow morning. :rocket: 

mike_cs: Marking owners in the folder and will ping when slides are ready.

raj: All results and a short readme uploaded. Last message ts: 3618890450 — let me know if you want extra slices.

sara: This is great — closing the loop. We'll use this for the renewal briefing. Thanks team. :white_check_mark:
